notes.title: Principal Component Regression
notes.excerpt: OLS blows up under multicollinearity across nearby channels. PCR fixes it by orthogonalizing features first, but the fix is blind to the target — which is exactly the failure mode PLS was built to avoid.

notes.title: Partial Least Squares
notes.excerpt: PLS is a regression technique that finds latent variables that maximize covariance between features and targets. It is particularly useful when features are highly collinear, as it avoids the pitfalls of OLS and PCR by considering the target variable during dimensionality reduction.

notes.title: Locked Image Text Tuning
notes.excerpt: Locked Image Text Tuning is a technique for fine-tuning image-text models by locking the image encoder and only updating the text encoder.

notes.title: SiGLIP: A Simple Generalized Language-Image Pre-training Approach
notes.excerpt: SiGLIP is a simple generalized language-image pre-training approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance on various multimodal tasks.

notes.title: Self Distillation for Local to Global Consistency (SiLC) and TIPS
notes.excerpt: SiLC and TIPS are techniques for self-distillation that improve consistency between local and global representations in multimodal models.

notes.title: Understanding the Q-Former in BLIP-2
notes.excerpt: The Q-Former is a key component in BLIP-2 that enables effective communication between the image and text modalities.

notes.title: Pixel Shuffle Method for VLMs Reducing Tokens
notes.excerpt: The Pixel Shuffle method is a technique used in vision-language models (VLMs) to reduce the number of tokens by rearranging the spatial dimensions of feature maps, leading to more efficient processing.

notes.title: Continuous to Discrete Tokenization for VLMs to VLA
notes.excerpt: Continuous to Discrete Tokenization is a method for converting continuous representations in vision-language models (VLMs) to discrete tokens, facilitating the transition from VLMs to vision-language agents (VLA) for tasks such as robotics.
